summary: The source owner is the whole uhitm.c:mhitm_ad_tlpt() helper, including all three attacker/defender identity branches, dispatched by the AD_TLPT arm of mhitm_adtyping(). In this case a landed hostile Quantum Mechanic attack reaches the monster-to-hero arm. JS refuses that AD_TLPT arm during cloned turn preflight, which becomes a turn-boundary stop before the live monster scan. The comparator’s earlier distfleeck RNG absence is a consequence of that preflight stop, not the source owner. The debug-wizard recording selects the hero’s current square, so it exercises the controlled teleport selector without claiming relocation.

source.branch: Port the complete mhitm_ad_tlpt() identity dispatch: magr == &youmonst (hero-to-monster), mdef == &youmonst (monster-to-hero), and otherwise monster-to-monster. This recording reaches the monster-to-hero arm only after the hostile AT_CLAW attack is in range, not skipped or missed by mattacku() hit gating, hitmu() rolls damage, AD_TLPT dispatches, and mhitm_mgc_atk_negated() permits the effect. The arm then calls tele(); wizard mode admits a controlled destination and the recorded selector chooses the current square. Preserve all arm conditions and damage caps; do not infer that the hero moved.
callers: uhitm.c:mhitm_adtyping() case AD_TLPT is the direct dispatch; its JavaScript counterpart is js/uhitm.js:4949, currently unported.
mhitu.c:mattacku() -> hitmu() -> mhitm_adtyping() is the reached monster-to-hero route; the claw hit gate is at mhitu.c:793-814 and hitmu dispatches after damage at mhitu.c:1187-1191.
mhitm.c:mdamagem() -> mhitm_adtyping() reaches the helper’s monster-to-monster arm at mhitm.c:1059.
uhitm.c:damageum() -> mhitm_adtyping() reaches the helper’s hero-to-monster arm at uhitm.c:4854.
dependencies: Direct shared dependency uhitm.c:mhitm_mgc_atk_negated(); a JavaScript implementation exists at js/uhitm.js:785.
Monster-to-hero dependency mhitu.c:hitmsg(); a JavaScript implementation exists at js/mhitu.js:654.

Monster-to-hero teleport dependency teleport.c:tele() -> scrolltele(), getpos(), teleok(), teleds(); JavaScript implementations are in js/teleport.js, including tele() at :1671 and scrolltele() at :1604. Audit this return closure during implementation.

The other complete-helper arms call teleport.c:u_teleport_mon(), tele_restrict(), and rloc(); JavaScript implementations exist in js/teleport.js at :508, :757, and :462. Audit their return closure during implementation.
Other AD_* arms in uhitm.c:mhitm_adtyping() remain separate unported attack-type paths; only its AD_TLPT arm is in this helper’s dispatch scope.

evidence: The immutable queue capsule `.cache/v19-investigation-capsules/0.json` records the exact evaluated commit 8583a972f66a872a8ad73c888a24dd01075481f4, manifest identity, recording SHA-256 bba42c7bc0af0cb19257439f57b65e5de23ea90f687fc5dc68b4f4bf5a3f4922, 61 steps, 21 remaining screens, and the stop `simple monster action requires uhitm.c mhitm_ad_tlpt()` at step 40. The v19 evaluation artifact for that commit reports 40/61 screens and cursors and 6259/6297 RNG calls.

The source definition `nethack-c/upstream/include/monsters.h:2127-2133` gives Quantum Mechanic one `AT_CLAW/AD_TLPT` attack with 1d4 damage. In `mhitu.c:mattacku()` at :793-814, the physical attack is omitted on its explicit gates or reaches `hitmu()` only on `tmp > rnd(20+i)`; a miss calls `missmu()`. `mhitu.c:hitmu()` rolls damage then calls `mhitm_adtyping()` at :1187-1191. The frozen C trace records “The quantum mechanic hits!”, `rnd(20)=8`, `d(1,4)=4`, and `rn2(10)=7` at `mhitm_mgc_atk_negated`, establishing this case passed target-miss and magic-negation gates.

The whole C helper is `nethack-c/upstream/src/uhitm.c:mhitm_ad_tlpt()` at :2859-2955; `mhitm_adtyping()` dispatches AD_TLPT to it at :4782-4802. The monster-to-hero arm at :2884-2927 calls `hitmsg()`, checks magic negation, messages uncertainty, calls `tele()`, then caps damage against polymorph HP or hero HP while preserving at least one HP. The helper also has hero-to-monster and monster-to-monster arms, so the source goal is the full helper, with only its AD_TLPT caller arm wired—not all attack types in `mhitm_adtyping()`.

For this debug-wizard input, `teleport.c:scrolltele()` allows controlled destination selection when `wizard` is set even without Teleport_control (`:872-892`); C then accepts the recorded current-square choice and reports “You materialize in the same location!” at step 48. This proves the selector path is reached but does not prove relocation; coordinates remain unchanged.

The JavaScript sequence is `allmain.js:1334-1336` calling `planElapsedTurn()` before its live `movemon()` loop at :1373-1377. `planElapsedTurn()` calls `preflightSimpleMonsterActions()` at :1242-1260; that function clones state and ISAAC (`js/unported_monster_actions.js:1780-1786`, `:364-367`). During the clone scan the JS `mhitm_adtyping()` AD_TLPT arm calls `unported()` (`js/uhitm.js:4949`), raising `UnsupportedSimpleMonsterActionError`; the preflight catch converts it to `UnsupportedTurnBoundaryError` (`js/allmain.js:1261-1276`). The live scan therefore never runs for this step.

Counter-evidence against treating `distfleeck` as owner: the older C62 raw comparator receipt in the capsule (run-ppCadc, measured worker head 3b30ca493456d7d79d49c1bf3ca79d9d32addf15; receipt SHA-256 f8ab7945d23fa41a51df2457f2c1912fbff0753971dbbcf23affcd95611b1cb2) reports C’s first absent-from-JS raw call as `rn2(5)=1` at `monmove.c:538`, input step 40. That is the live scan’s earlier call; the cloned preflight RNG is discarded after the AD_TLPT refusal, before live `movemon()`. The receipt’s measured commit is older than this investigation’s evaluation commit, so it supports the raw symptom only; source and current evaluation establish the cause.
